fragments.purpose: Talk cover: title and author on an accent fill
Deck opening with one dominant title
Chapter divider with the number from the outline
Standalone finding, frame or bridge in one sentence
Short points united by one question or finding
Two states or options on a shared basis
Image as evidence, with a short note on what to look at
Quantitative relationship with a finding and a source
Exact comparison of records of the same kind
Source code whose specific lines prove a technical finding
Handoff, dependency or transformation between nodes
Closing line, author with event and one contact as a QR code
Set of equal topics on one page: tiles of equal height in a row
Full-slide screenshot, screen recording or long page with a title that leaves
Current interface version large, earlier iterations beside it

title.job: Open the talk with its topic instead of proving a claim
useWhen: first slide of material without a speaker: a handout deck, a recording, an internal review
avoidWhen: this is a public talk; use cover for that
you need a transition between sections
the title already states a substantive finding
variable: title length up to two lines
local fill and a meta line when needed
fixed: one dominant title
no list, diagram or secondary argument

slots.TITLE: Title of the talk or standalone material

reveal.guidance: The title slide shows in full.

alternatives.cover: for a talk with an author
alternatives.statement: for a claim inside the story

cover.job: Open the talk with the title, the author and the character of the topic
useWhen: this is the public cover of a talk
the audience should see the author or event name before the talk starts
avoidWhen: you need a neutral title card inside the material
the slide must already prove a claim
variable: title on one or two lines
fixed: the title dominates
meta details do not compete with the topic

slots.TITLE: Talk title
slots.BYLINE: Author, optionally followed by a dot and the event

reveal.guidance: The cover shows in full.

alternatives.title: for a neutral opening without an author line
alternatives.section: for a transition inside the talk

context.job: Briefly explain who is speaking and why their experience matters for the topic
useWhen: the audience does not know the speaker
role or hands-on experience affects trust in the material
avoidWhen: the bio does not help understand the talk
the context fits in one spoken sentence
variable: name, role and one reason for expertise
fixed: only facts related to the topic
one visual anchor

slots.relevance: Why this experience matters for the topic

reveal.guidance: The context slide shows in full.

alternatives.figure: if the project or result matters more than the person
alternatives.title: if no introduction is needed

section.job: Mark the move to a new part of the story
useWhen: the question or scale of the story changes
the audience needs a short pause between blocks
avoidWhen: the slide holds a standalone argument
the section is just the next single slide
fixed: minimum content
no evidence and no explanatory lists

slots.SECTION_TITLE: Chapter title, word for word as in the outline

reveal.guidance: The divider has no reveal steps.

alternatives.title: for the start of the whole deck

list.job: Group a few short points that together support one heading
useWhen: the points are equal or follow a simple spoken order
each point makes sense without axes or links
avoidWhen: the points have dates
the points are steps of an instruction
causal or spatial links between items matter
fixed: all points are of one kind
one heading explains how they relate

slots.SLIDE_TITLE: Finding or question that unites the points
slots.LIST_ITEMS: List items with the same internal structure

reveal.guidance: For reading together, show everything. If the speaker goes through the points one by one, the first frame shows the heading, with the first point if needed. The remaining points get .frag; a label and its note appear together.

statement.job: State one finding or turn in the argument
useWhen: the wording must land on its own
the evidence is already shown or comes on the next slide
avoidWhen: the claim needs several caveats
the slide is only a section title
variable: a neutral fill for a frame, a bridge or a fact; `surface-accent` for the finding the audience takes away
fixed: one thought
the claim stays the main object on the slide

reveal.guidance: The claim shows in full.

alternatives.figure: if an image must back the finding right away

comparison.job: Compare two states or two options on a shared basis
useWhen: both sides answer one question
the difference reads through the same criteria or images
avoidWhen: the columns hold unrelated topics
you need to show more than two options
a numeric scale shows the change better
variable: text, metrics or images inside the sides
accent on the side the claim singles out; equal options stay neutral
fixed: two comparable areas
both sides read the same way
the shared criterion and comparable values are named; use Before / After only for a change in one object
two independent topics do not become a comparison just because there are two columns

slots.LEFT_CONTENT: First state with its own label
slots.RIGHT_CONTENT: Second state with the same structure

reveal.guidance: Reveal the second side later only if the speaker goes through the first one first.

alternatives.table: for three or more options or exact values

quote.job: Give a short outside quote weight of its own
useWhen: the exact words of the source matter more than a paraphrase
the quote turns the argument or confirms a conflict
avoidWhen: the phrase is trite
the author or source is unknown
the quote needs a long explanation
variable: quote on one or two lines
fixed: verified, word-for-word wording
visible attribution

reveal.guidance: Quote and author appear together.

alternatives.figure: for a screenshot of the original source

metrics.job: Show a few big numbers that together prove one finding
useWhen: each metric makes sense without a shared axis
two, three or four numbers describe one scale or result
avoidWhen: the metrics cannot be compared or tied to one claim
change over periods matters
the numbers are only for reference
variable: units, short labels and a source
fixed: one heading ties all numbers together
each label explains what the value means

slots.title: Shared finding
slots.metrics: Values with units and short labels

reveal.guidance: If the metrics are revealed, the first frame shows the heading, with the first metric if needed. The rest get .frag.

alternatives.chart: for relationships on a shared scale
alternatives.table: for an exact set of many values

code.job: Show the source lines a technical finding rests on
useWhen: the audience must see specific syntax or a condition
the snippet fits without shrinking the font
avoidWhen: the code is only a backdrop
how the interface works matters, not the implementation
the snippet needs long line-by-line reading
fixed: the code stays readable
highlighting points to the lines of the argument

reveal.guidance: To shift focus, use neighboring slides with the same code, but never an empty first frame.

alternatives.figure: for the result of running the code

figure.job: Make an image, diagram or screenshot the main evidence
useWhen: the finding is visible in the image
a short caption helps notice the right detail
avoidWhen: the image is decoration
the caption retells the whole image
the media reads better full-slide
variable: local annotations on top of the media
fixed: the media takes the main area
the text says where to look

slots.SLIDE_TITLE: Finding or context of the image

reveal.guidance: Annotations may be revealed, but the image is visible on the first frame.

screenshot.job: Show a screen, a screen recording or a long page across the whole slide
useWhen: interface details must be large
the result is visible only in motion: use a recording
a long page does not shrink into a readable frame: use .shot--scroll
avoidWhen: the media needs a long explanation beside it
you need to compare two states
the recording runs longer than twenty seconds without editing
variable: a title that leaves after three seconds or stays
fixed: the media covers the whole slide
the title hangs from the top edge in the middle
a video has a poster and preload="none"

slots.MEDIA: ,
slots.SLIDE_TITLE: What the audience is looking at

reveal.guidance: The media shows on the first frame. A title with data-exit="intended" leaves after three seconds; keep the attribute unless the title must stay.

table.job: Give an exact comparison of records of the same kind
useWhen: specific values matter
the reader must cross-check rows and columns
avoidWhen: one visual finding is enough
the table needs small text
rows have different internal structure
variable: number of rows and columns within readability
fixed: column headings
dataset caption
every row follows the same logic

reveal.guidance: Show the table in full as a rule. Revealing rows gets in the way of comparison.

alternatives.chart: if the shape of the difference matters more than each number

steps.job: Show a prescribed sequence of actions
useWhen: the stages must be done in the given order
each step has an action and a short result
avoidWhen: these are past events with dates
the arrows describe data handoff
the points can be reordered without losing meaning
variable: title and short description for each step
fixed: the order is part of the meaning
all items describe actions of one process

reveal.guidance: If the steps are revealed, the first frame shows the heading, with the first step if needed. The remaining steps get .frag.

chart.job: Show a quantitative relationship that proves the finding
useWhen: the data can be shown honestly on a shared scale
the shape or difference matters more than the full set of exact values
avoidWhen: the data is not numeric
geography, a network or a distribution loses meaning in a standard chart
the reader needs exact values for many rows
variable: number of categories and series within readability
scales, labels, source and the highlighted item
a local subject-specific visualization instead of a ready-made form
fixed: the heading or a nearby block states one finding
the visualization has an accessible text description
color and accent follow Craft roles

slots.CHART_SUMMARY: Text description of the data and the finding
slots.FINDING: Short finding next to the chart

reveal.guidance: If the finding is revealed later, the chart is already visible on the first frame.

alternatives.figure: for a subject diagram or map

timeline.job: Show how events changed the state over time
useWhen: the events have dates or periods
chronological order explains the outcome
avoidWhen: the points are an instruction
time does not affect the finding
you need to show numeric change
fixed: time marks
chronological order

reveal.guidance: If the events are revealed, the first frame shows only the heading. Every event, including the first, gets .frag.

alternatives.flow: for how a system is built

flow.job: Show handoff, dependency or transformation between nodes
useWhen: the arrow has a concrete meaning
the node order describes the path of an object or signal
avoidWhen: the items are just listed
the nodes are events in time
the links do not matter for the finding
variable: optional accent on the node the claim singles out, wherever it sits
concrete link labels in a local composition
fixed: each link means handoff, dependency or transformation; spoken order is not a link
nodes on one level read as parts of one system
all nodes are neutral by default; a central position does not earn an accent
flow-node--accent is a fixed highlight; deck.js does not move it during reveal

slots.SLIDE_TITLE: Finding about the path or the structure of the system
slots.FLOW_NODES: Nodes and links with explicit direction

reveal.guidance: For an overview, show everything. To explain a path, the first frame shows the heading and the start node. Each next .frag combines the incoming link with the next node. A branch appears after its source, a return link after both ends. Never leave an arrow pointing at nothing.

visual-comparison.job: Compare two images on a shared basis
useWhen: the difference is visible directly in two frames
both sides can be shown at the same scale
avoidWhen: the images show different objects
the difference needs a table of criteria
annotating one frame is enough
variable: late reveal of the second side
fixed: both halves follow the same logic
comparable image scale

reveal.guidance: The second side may be revealed later if the first already makes a meaningful frame.

resource.job: Hand the audience one specific resource
useWhen: the resource is needed right after the related part of the talk
a working QR code opens the address
avoidWhen: the slide has several unrelated links
the resource is unverified or unavailable
this is the final contact slide with no separate material
variable: screenshot or short description of the resource
fixed: one resource
the address is repeated as text

slots.title: What the audience gets
slots.qr: QR code for the same address

reveal.guidance: Resource, address and QR code appear together.

alternatives.figure: if the resource is evidence rather than a handout

end.job: Close the story with a final statement and give the next contact
useWhen: this is the last slide of the deck
the audience should take away one statement or address
avoidWhen: arguments still remain
someone tries to fit several resources on the slide
variable: one contact as a QR code with its address
fixed: closing line in the middle, author bottom left, QR code bottom right
no slide number
one contact

slots.AUTHOR: Author as on the cover
slots.EVENT: Event name, empty if there is none

reveal.guidance: The final slide shows in full.

alternatives.statement: for a finding before the end of the talk

bento.job: Show a whole set on one page: a stack, a set of topics, areas of work
useWhen: there are more than six equal topics
the size and makeup matter, not a walk through each topic
avoidWhen: the topics are covered one by one
the items have an order or links
a tile needs a description
variable: tile width --span out of twelve columns
one .is-accent tile if the claim singles it out
fixed: one topic per tile, no descriptions
tiles in a row have equal height
one page without .frag

reveal.guidance: No reveal steps. Tiles appear in a short stagger when entering forward; on return and in print they show at once.

alternatives.list: for three to five topics covered one by one

iterations.job: Show how the interface changed, with the current version in focus
useWhen: three or more versions of one screen
the path matters, not a before/after pair
avoidWhen: there are two versions; use visual-comparison for them
the screens are different
variable: captions with a date or stage
fixed: current version large on the left
captions above the frames
frames of one screen at one scale

slots.ITERATIONS: <figure class="iteration is-current"> and earlier <figure class="iteration"> with figcaption and .frame

reveal.guidance: Earlier iterations may be revealed one at a time; the current one is visible on the first frame.

alternatives.timeline: if dates matter more than looks

catalogExamples.name: Talk cover
catalogExamples.job: Title and author open a public talk
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use as the first frame of a talk with clear authorship
catalogExamples.variable: Change the title, author line and brand motif, but do not add arguments

catalogExamples.name: Speaker context
catalogExamples.job: Role and experience explain the author's link to the topic
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use only when the bio affects trust in the material
catalogExamples.variable: Change the portrait, role and the one reason for expertise

catalogExamples.name: Divider
catalogExamples.job: A short pause marks a new block of the story
catalogExamples.useWhen: Put it between major parts, not before every subsection
catalogExamples.variable: Change the title, number and local motif

catalogExamples.name: Outline
catalogExamples.job: A list shows the route of a long talk up front
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when the audience benefits from knowing the talk structure
catalogExamples.variable: Change the number of points and the reveal, but keep the outline to one level

catalogExamples.name: Claim
catalogExamples.job: One statement gets the whole slide
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for a finding or a turn in the argument
catalogExamples.variable: Change the fill and the short qualifier

catalogExamples.name: Argument list
catalogExamples.job: Several points support a shared heading
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for equal arguments with no geometry of their own
catalogExamples.variable: Change the marker, length and reveal within readability

catalogExamples.name: Text comparison
catalogExamples.job: Two states compared by the same criteria
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for states of one object or two options with a shared criterion, not for independent points
catalogExamples.variable: Change the content of the sides, keep the shared structure

catalogExamples.name: Quote
catalogExamples.job: A verified outside quote turns or confirms the argument
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use only when the exact words and the author matter
catalogExamples.variable: Change the length and attribution, keeping the quote within two lines

catalogExamples.name: Big metrics
catalogExamples.job: Several numbers together describe one result
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for two, three or four self-contained metrics
catalogExamples.variable: Change the count, units and accent, but do not turn the block into a table

catalogExamples.name: Code
catalogExamples.job: Specific source lines prove a technical finding
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when the audience must see the syntax or a condition
catalogExamples.variable: Change the language, context and focus lines

catalogExamples.name: Media with a note
catalogExamples.job: The image is the evidence, the text guides the eye
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for a diagram, photo or subject visualization with a short finding
catalogExamples.variable: Change the column proportions, the media and the annotation

catalogExamples.name: Full-screen screenshot
catalogExamples.job: The screen fills the slide, the title stays
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when interface details must be as large as possible
catalogExamples.variable: Change the cropping and the one caption

catalogExamples.name: Data table
catalogExamples.job: Rows and columns compare exact values
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when the audience needs specific numbers
catalogExamples.variable: Change rows and columns until the text would have to shrink

catalogExamples.name: Steps
catalogExamples.job: Actions form a prescribed sequence
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for a process that must be done in order
catalogExamples.variable: Change the number of steps, the descriptions and the current stage

catalogExamples.name: Categories and finding
catalogExamples.job: A horizontal scale compares categories with long names
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when the order or the difference between categories matters
catalogExamples.variable: Change the number of rows, the scale and the highlight; for other kinds of data pick another form

catalogExamples.name: Value by period
catalogExamples.job: Bars show one value across discrete periods
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when the periods have a natural order
catalogExamples.variable: Change the number of periods, the scale and the accent bar

catalogExamples.name: Continuous change
catalogExamples.job: A line shows the shape of continuous change and the turning point
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for sequential observations where the slope matters
catalogExamples.variable: Change the points, one main and one background series, and the end labels

catalogExamples.name: Parts of a whole
catalogExamples.job: A ring shows the makeup of one whole
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use only for two, three or four distinct parts of one total
catalogExamples.variable: Change the parts, the key order and the highlighted part

catalogExamples.name: Makeup by period
catalogExamples.job: Stacked bars show how the parts of one whole change
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when each period adds up to a total
catalogExamples.variable: Change the periods and up to four parts, keeping the color order

catalogExamples.name: Two series by period
catalogExamples.job: Paired bars compare two series within each period
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for two comparable values on a shared scale
catalogExamples.variable: Change the periods, values and the highlighted series

catalogExamples.name: Change between measurements
catalogExamples.job: Each row shows how a value moved between two points
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for a before/after comparison across several categories
catalogExamples.variable: Change the categories, both measurements and the focus row

catalogExamples.name: Timeline
catalogExamples.job: Dated events explain the current state
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when time is part of the argument
catalogExamples.variable: Change the number of events, the periods and the current point

catalogExamples.name: Flow diagram
catalogExamples.job: Arrows show handoff or transformation between nodes
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when every link has a concrete meaning
catalogExamples.variable: Change the direction, branching and nodes to match the real links. Neutral nodes are the default; the accent is not tied to the center

catalogExamples.name: Image comparison
catalogExamples.job: Two frames show the visual difference before and after
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for comparable images at the same scale
catalogExamples.variable: Change the captions, cropping and reveal order

catalogExamples.name: Title card
catalogExamples.job: A neutral card opens standalone material or a short deck
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use without an author line or a decorative cover
catalogExamples.variable: Change the title and the fill

catalogExamples.name: Takeaways
catalogExamples.job: A short list brings the main findings back to the audience
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use near the end, after the evidence
catalogExamples.variable: Change the number of takeaways and the reveal, keeping each one self-contained

catalogExamples.name: Resource
catalogExamples.job: A preview, an address and a QR code hand over one piece of material
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for a verified link the audience needs
catalogExamples.variable: Change the preview and the address, but do not combine several resources

catalogExamples.name: Bento
catalogExamples.job: A whole set on one page: tiles appear in a stagger
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for a stack or a set of topics you will not cover one by one
catalogExamples.variable: Change the number of rows and the tile widths

catalogExamples.name: Interface iterations
catalogExamples.job: Current version large, earlier ones beside it
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for three or more versions of one screen
catalogExamples.variable: Change the number of earlier iterations and the captions

catalogExamples.name: Typed command
catalogExamples.job: The command types itself, the output comes out line by line
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use when running a command and its result matter
catalogExamples.variable: Change the command lines in data-run-commands

catalogExamples.name: Wipe
catalogExamples.job: A boundary slides across one frame from the old look to the new one
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for two states of one screen at one scale
catalogExamples.variable: Change the final boundary position --wipe

catalogExamples.name: Long screenshot
catalogExamples.job: The header stays put while the content scrolls
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use for a long page that cannot shrink into a readable frame
catalogExamples.variable: Change the --scroll-duration

catalogExamples.name: Ending
catalogExamples.job: The last thought and one contact close the talk
catalogExamples.useWhen: Use as the last slide
catalogExamples.variable: Change the final statement, the contact and the working QR code
